prompt: You step out of a dark cinema into bright sunshine, and your pupils quickly change size. What happens, and why?

options.text: They get larger, to gather more light for the retina
They get smaller, to limit the light entering the eye
They get larger, to cool the eye down
They stay the same size; only the lens changes

explanation: In bright light the iris makes the pupil smaller, reducing the light entering the eye and protecting the retina — the pupillary light reflex.
